says: Rebuilding the walker as a body, not tubes: the torso leans further into the wind, the front knee bends forward over the boot, the legs swell at thigh and calf and narrow at knee and ankle, the back arm bends at a visible elbow, and its hand now has fingers. The ribs are now tapered bone rising from a half-buried chain of vertebrae, thinning toward their tips, one snapped short, stippled on the shadow side with pits and cracks, no more bamboo bands. The pentagons and circles are gone from the ground; a few small irregular stones are shaded and shadowed on one side, and the walker cast shadow is hatched and starts at the feet.
